With the server costs becoming exponentially higher as a result of heavier traffic, the site is at a crossroads. Scale down and then try to rebuild up again slower or roll with the punches and scale the business model to accommodate more users. With the unique situation that lead to Reddit's predicament and the media coverage of both it and Voat, I do not see the site growing well if it does decide to wait until all the media upheaval blows over. We have people saying about subscriptions and so forth but these ideas will inhibit growth and as content is the sites selling point, we need user growth. So here are my proposals:

  • Short of business investment advertising is the only legitimate short term solution to the sites funding issues. 10k Euros a month server costs isn't something that the current userbase can support. Non-intrusive but visible and I'm sure the userbase will support the Admins by whitelisting the site in order to fund the server costs.

  • Use the revenue to maintain current scale-up of the userbase and in turn content, whilst both continuing discussions with investors and building a small team of operators to support the scale up and feature development.

  • The user-friendly spin - The top voted comments from the month, or another defined period of time, are given a percentage of net profits from the site. This gives both some of the ad revenue back into the community, for genuinely positive contributions to the community. This gives the users a sense of power (deciding top contributors to pay) and promotes good, well thought out comments.

  • Voat Gold (name should be decided by user poll - it gives users a sense of ownership/democratic input into the site.) This gives a percentage (50/50?) of the price it costs to the site and part to the recipient. People can be directly paid for quality content submitted to the site which in turn, increases the amount of quality content.

  • Atko/putitout - you have thousands of individuals using the site currently, some are no doubt lawyers, some teachers, but some will be the very people who can help develop features for the site. Reach out to them, ask for their help and create a group of volunteers who speed up development of a certain feature, something small but productive. Reward them with a special identifier or badge so everyone knows they're helping develop the site.

These ideas are by no means polished answers the the sites issues but they show the direction we need to be thinking in. Democratic, user-rewarding and financially viable while supporting user growth. It cannot be stressed enough though that waiting in limbo and letting the opportunity blow over, in the hope that the site can be scaled up slower, is not the direction to go.
